curriculum: Common Core, opened: K.OA.A.1-2 (represent and solve within 10 with objects, drawings, fingers, equations), K.OA.A.3-5 (decompositions, make-ten partner, fluency within 5) [ccss-koa]; 1.OA.A.1-2 (word problems within 20, three addends), 1.OA.B.4 (subtraction as unknown addend), 1.OA.C.5-6 (counting on; fluency within 10, make-ten and decomposition within 20), 1.OA.D.8 (unknown in an equation) [ccss-1oa]; 1.NBT.C.4-6 (add within 100, 10 more/less, subtract multiples of ten) [ccss-1nbt]; 2.OA.A.1 (one- and two-step problems within 100), 2.OA.B.2 (fluency within 20) [ccss-2oa]; 2.NBT.B.5-9 (within 100 and 1000, explain why strategies work) [ccss-2nbt]; 3.NBT.A.2 (within 1000) [ccss-3nbt].

brief.json lists '1.OA, 2.OA.A-B, 1.NBT.C.4-6, 2.NBT.B.5-9, 3.NBT.A.2' which all exist. Note 2.OA.B is only 2.OA.B.2 (there is no B.3-4; 2.OA.C.3-4 are odd/even and arrays and belong elsewhere). 1.OA.B.3 (properties) belongs to properties-of-operations and 1.OA.D.7 to equality-equal-sign.

England PoS, opened: Year 1 read/write/interpret + - = statements, number bonds within 20, add/subtract one- and two-digit numbers to 20, one-step and missing-number problems with objects and pictures; Year 2 recall facts to 20, derive facts to 100, commutativity of addition (not subtraction), inverse for checking and missing numbers, add three one-digit numbers; Year 3 mentally add/subtract 3-digit with ones, tens, hundreds, estimate and use inverse; Y4 four-digit; Y5 more than four digits [eng-pos]. Brief's 'Y1-Y5' confirmed. Formal columnar method is statutory from Year 3 (Year 2 notes only mention recording in columns); this concerns column-addition-subtraction.
Korea 2022: not opened (vivasam and goe.go.kr PDFs returned only binary or grade 5-6 content). Codes [2수01-05..07] therefore unverified.
textbooks: IM Grade 1 Unit 1: fluency within 10 mainly through centers, counting on/back by 1 or 2, two-color counters and ten frames [im-g1].

IM Grade 1 Unit 2: story problems within 10, problem types Add To, Take From, Put Together/Take Apart, Compare, Change Unknown with the unknown in several positions; boxes for unknowns; many equations may fit one story [im-g1].

IM Grade 1 Unit 3: ten as a unit of 10 ones; Section A within 10 using counting on and making ten, ten frames showing 8+2=10 and 10-2=8; B teen numbers on double ten frames; C add within 20 by grouping to make ten, including three addends, near doubles (7+7 for 7+8); D subtract within 20 by taking away to ten, counting on to ten, using the addition fact (6+4=10 for 10-6) [im-g1].

IM Grade 1 Unit 5: add within 100, compare adding on by place with adding like units; connecting cubes in tens and ones and base-ten drawings; equations written horizontally to keep thinking about numbers; compare three named children's methods for 37+25 [im-g1].

IM Grade 2 Unit 7: Section A add/subtract within 1000 without composing/decomposing (compare, count on/back, tens and hundreds); B add using place value, compose a ten or hundred; C subtract using place value, decompose a ten or hundred; the lessons page does not say which representations appear [im-g2u7].

IM Grade 3 Unit 3: addition and subtraction within 1000 with base-ten blocks and diagrams, expanded form, vertical partial sums; rounding on number lines; tape diagrams with equations; two-step problems [im-g3].

OpenStax Prealgebra 2e 1.3 Add Whole Numbers: notation, base-ten blocks (units and rods, exchange ten ones for a ten), vertical layout from right to left, carrying described as the same as regrouping by exchanging, addition fact table to memorise, identity and commutative properties, translating key words (sum, increased by, more than, total of, added to), four-step word-problem plan [os-add].

OpenStax Prealgebra 2e 1.4 Subtract Whole Numbers: minus as take away, difference; blocks with exchange of a ten for ten ones (called borrowing, also exchange or regrouping); check by adding back; key words (decreased by, less than, subtracted from) with reversal of order for 'less than' and 'subtracted from'; examples 7-3, 43-26, 910-586, 2162-479 [os-sub].
explanations: Objects and fingers (direct modelling: count all, take away): [ccss-koa], [prog-oa].
Ten frames and two-color counters, double ten frames for teen numbers: [im-g1].
Counting on / counting back, and counting on as the way to subtract (unknown addend): [prog-oa Level 2], [ccss-1oa 1.OA.B.4, 1.OA.C.5].
Making ten and decomposing (8+6 = 8+2+4), near doubles (6+7 = 6+6+1), described as converting to an easier problem: [prog-oa Level 3], [ccss-1oa 1.OA.C.6], [im-g1 Unit 3].

Part-part-whole and bar/tape diagram, number bonds: [prog-oa], [ncetm-as] (segments 1.2 introducing part-part-whole, 1.5 aggregation and partitioning, 1.6 augmentation and reduction, 1.12 subtraction as difference).
Base-ten blocks / connecting cubes and base-ten drawings with exchange: [im-g1 Unit 5], [im-g3 Unit 3], [os-add], [os-sub].

Number line for difference and rounding: [im-g3 Unit 3 uses number lines for rounding]; use of a number line for compensation 28+16 as 30+14: [nrich-bal]. Number line for addition itself: unverified in opened pages.
Words and symbols: sum, difference, plus, minus, key-phrase translation: [os-add], [os-sub].
conventions: Regrouping vocabulary: OpenStax uses carry, regroup, exchange and borrow side by side for the same step [os-add, os-sub]; NCETM column-addition page says 'regroup' and the Year 3 column-subtraction pages say 'exchange' and not 'borrow' [ncetm-cadd, ncetm-y3u7]; IM says compose / decompose a ten [im-g2u7].

Terms: addend and sum (OpenStax); minuend and subtrahend appear in NCETM Year 3 outcomes [ncetm-y3u7] but OpenStax 1.4 does not define them [os-sub]. Problem types are named Add To / Take From / Put Together-Take Apart / Compare in CCSS and IM [prog-oa, im-g1].
Layout: IM Grade 1 writes equations horizontally on purpose [im-g1]; OpenStax stacks vertically with carries written above the next column [os-add].
Korean number words and the words for plus/minus (sino-Korean 일, 이, 삼 versus native 하나, 둘, 셋; 더하기, 빼기): unverified, no Korean source was opened.
Equal sign: US 'equal sign', England 'equals sign' [cm-eq says 'equal sign'; eng-pos says 'equals sign'].
misconceptions: Treating = as 'now write the answer' when sums are in unusual positions: see equality-equal-sign [nrich-bal, cm-eq].
Compare problems with misleading 'more'/'fewer' wording are among the hardest for children; the progression says mastery is expected only in Grade 2 [prog-oa].
Order matters in word translation: 'less than' and 'subtracted from' reverse the written order [os-sub].
Subtraction is not commutative; England expects Year 2 pupils to show addition can be reordered but subtraction cannot [eng-pos].

Teaching advice: IM stresses explaining how an equation matches the story over matching a particular method, and that several equations can fit one story [im-g1]. NCETM presents addition and subtraction as related operations and teaches structures (aggregation, augmentation, partitioning, reduction, comparison) [ncetm-as, titles only].

Gelman and Gallistel counting principles, subitizing as base for adding: not opened here (belongs to counting-number-names); the progression mentions that the last number said gives the quantity and supports counting on [prog-oa].
tasks: Join / separate / part-part-whole / compare word problems within 10, 20, 100, with unknown in any position [ccss-1oa 1.OA.A.1, ccss-2oa 2.OA.A.1].
Find the partner to 10, decompose within 10 [ccss-koa K.OA.A.3-4]; 8+2=10 and 10-2=8 on ten frames [im-g1].
Add three one-digit numbers; make ten with three addends [eng-pos Y2, im-g1].
Add and subtract 10 or 100 mentally within 100-900 [ccss-2nbt 2.NBT.B.8]; 37+25 by several methods [im-g1].
Two- and three-digit sums/differences with exchange, checked by the inverse [os-add, os-sub, eng-pos Y3].

Facts later concepts need: commutativity and inverse relation (properties-of-operations, equality-equal-sign), the place-value strategies leading to column methods (column-addition-subtraction), repeated addition as the start of multiplication (multiplication), subtraction as an unknown addend [ccss-1oa 1.OA.B.4].

curriculum: Common Core, opened: 4.NBT.B.4 requires fluent add/subtract of multi-digit whole numbers with the standard algorithm, the only standard that names the standard algorithm [ccss-4nbt]. Earlier: 2.NBT.B.7 within 1000 with place-value strategies connected to a written method, 2.NBT.B.9 explain why strategies work [ccss-2nbt]; 3.NBT.A.2 within 1000 [ccss-3nbt]. The footnote on 3.NBT says more than one algorithm may be used [ccss-3nbt].

England PoS, opened: Year 3 statutory add/subtract up to three digits using formal written methods of columnar addition and subtraction; Year 4 up to four digits 'where appropriate'; Year 5 more than four digits; Year 2 notes only say recording in columns prepares for formal methods. Brief's 'Y2-Y5' should read Y3-Y5 for statutory use (Y2 as preparation) [eng-pos]. Appendix 1 (written methods) not opened.
Korea 2022 [2수01-06..07]: not opened; unverified.
textbooks: IM Grade 2 Unit 7 (add, then subtract within 1000, composing and decomposing tens and hundreds) [im-g2u7].

IM Grade 3 Unit 3: Section A addition with place value and properties, B subtraction using expanded form and moving toward streamlined notation that leads to the standard algorithm; vertical partial sums; base-ten blocks and diagrams [im-g3].

OpenStax Prealgebra 2e 1.3-1.4: blocks, then stacked numbers by place value, right to left, small carry digit above the next column, borrowing when a top digit is smaller; examples 17+26, 21,357+861+8,596, 207-64, 910-586, 2,162-479 [os-add, os-sub].

NCETM Spine 1: Year 3 segments 1.20 column addition and 1.21 column subtraction; Year 3 unit outcomes include naming minuend and subtrahend, exchange tens to ones and hundreds to tens, evaluating efficiency of strategies [ncetm-cadd, ncetm-csub, ncetm-y3u7].
explanations: Base-ten blocks with exchange of ten ones for one ten: [os-add], [os-sub], [im-g3].
Expanded form and vertical partial sums (add each place separately and then combine): [im-g3].
Streamlined column notation with carries: [os-add], [im-g3 'streamlined notation'].
Exchanging from the column to the left in subtraction (called exchange): [ncetm-y3u7].
Check by the inverse operation: [os-sub], [eng-pos].
Estimation before calculating: [eng-pos Y3 statutory].
conventions: Carry / regroup / exchange / borrow all used; OpenStax equates carrying with regrouping by exchanging [os-add]; NCETM avoids 'borrow' in the Year 3 pages and uses 'exchange' [ncetm-y3u7]; IM uses compose/decompose [im-g2u7].
Column names: ones, tens, hundreds; least significant digit is on the right [ncetm-cadd].

Layout: carries written as small digits above the next column (OpenStax) [os-add]; the placement of the exchange mark in subtraction in other countries, including the Korean layout of 받아올림/받아내림: unverified.
Thousands separators: OpenStax writes 21,357 with commas [os-add]; spaces/points used elsewhere: unverified.
misconceptions: The progression of Common Core allows several algorithms; the standard algorithm is required only by 4.NBT.B.4 and only for addition/subtraction [ccss-4nbt, ccss-3nbt footnote].
Digits must be aligned by place value, not by right edge of the written number text, and the work goes right to left [ncetm-cadd, os-add].

Subtracting the smaller digit from the larger regardless of position, and trouble with zeros in the top number: the pages opened do not list these; both are standard in the literature but unverified here. OpenStax example 910-586 and 207-64 are cases with a zero [os-sub].
NCETM says exchange should be explored in detail but lists no common errors in the pages opened [ncetm-y3u7].

Teaching advice: connect each written step to place-value strategies and explain why they work (2.NBT.B.7 and B.9) [ccss-2nbt]; IM keeps horizontal equations in Grade 1 to avoid rote algorithm before understanding [im-g1].
tasks: Two- and three-digit sums with and without carrying; sums with three or more addends [os-add].
Differences with one exchange, two exchanges, and a zero in the top number [os-sub].
Up to four digits (Y4), beyond four digits (Y5) [eng-pos].
Check a subtraction by adding back; estimate first [os-sub, eng-pos].
Needed later: long multiplication adds partial products in columns [os-mul]; decimal operations line up place values (brief later_concepts).

curriculum: Common Core, opened: 1.OA.D.7 understand the meaning of the equal sign and judge whether addition/subtraction equations are true or false; 1.OA.D.8 find the unknown in an equation with three whole numbers [ccss-1oa]. Brief lists '1.OA.D.7-8': confirmed. Also relevant: 2.OA.A.1 (symbol for the unknown) [ccss-2oa], 3.OA.A.4 (unknown in multiplication/division equation) and 3.OA.D.8 (letter for the unknown) [ccss-3oa], 4.NBT.A.2 uses =, < , > [ccss-4nbt], 6.EE.A.4 equivalent expressions [ccss-6ee].

England PoS, opened: Year 1 statutory read, write and interpret statements with +, - and =, and solve missing-number problems such as 7 = ? - 9; Year 2 missing numbers via the inverse; Year 4 notes: write statements of equality of expressions; Year 5 statutory 'understanding the meaning of the equals sign' and notes: equals sign for equivalence, e.g. 13+24 = 12+25 [eng-pos].
Korea [2수02-03], [4수02-xx]: not opened; unverified (and 2수02-03 may be a pattern or equation code; cannot confirm).
textbooks: IM Grade 1 Unit 2: the equal sign is a key focus; answer need not come after it; 7 = 5 + 2 is a valid statement; a box marks the unknown; unknown in several positions [im-g1].
OpenStax Prealgebra 2e 1.3: defines expression versus equation (3+4 is an expression, 3+4=7 an equation); the 'Introduction to Whole Numbers' module does not cover = [os-add, os-wn].
IM Grade 3 Unit 1 glossary: an equation shows that the expressions on both sides have the same value [im-g3u1gl].
explanations: Both sides have the same value ('is the same as'), also reading = as 'makes' only in the operational sense: [prog-oa], [cm-eq].
Total on the left (5 = 2 + 3) to show decompositions: [prog-oa].
Number balance and 'equivalent pairs' tasks; three-stage progression (answer-after-symbol only; both directions; full equivalence) citing Molina and Ambrose 2008: [nrich-bal].
True/false equations: [ccss-1oa 1.OA.D.7].
Properties of equality (reflexive, symmetric, transitive) taught on purpose: [cm-eq].
Substitutive meaning (replace one side by the other): [cm-eq].
conventions: 'equal sign' (US; Cambridge Maths advises it) versus 'equals sign' (England PoS wording) [eng-pos, cm-eq].
Unknown marks: box (IM), question mark (England PoS 7 = ? - 9), letter (CCSS 3.OA.D.8), underscore/blank in US problems [im-g1, eng-pos, ccss-3oa, nrich-bal].
Reading: Cambridge Maths suggests reading = as 'is the same as' [cm-eq]; the Korean word for = (등호; 같다) unverified.
Greater/less symbols with =: 2.NBT.A.4 and 4.NBT.A.2 [ccss-2nbt, ccss-4nbt].
misconceptions: Operational view: = means 'calculate/write the answer'; fails on 4 = 4, or 13 - 0 = 14 - 1; assumes sums read left to right [cm-eq].
8 + 4 = _ + 5: answers 12 (add left side only) or 17 (add all numbers) are the typical errors [nrich-bal, cm-eq].

Textbooks often show operations = answer: up to about 70% of the time in some US books, while Chinese students see more varied formats and do better on equivalence items [ca-eq summarising McNeil et al. 2006 and Li et al. 2008].
Operational conceptions linked to worse algebra performance in middle school (Knuth et al. 2006, as summarised) [ca-eq].

Teaching advice: teach relational meaning early (ages 5-7); vary formats such as 7 = 5 + 2; avoid materials that reinforce operations-then-answer only; draw attention to the = sign itself [cm-eq, ca-eq, im-g1].
tasks: True or false: 8 = 5 + 3, 3 + 4 = 4 + 3, 6 = 6, 5 + 2 = 2 + 5 style sentences [ccss-1oa 1.OA.D.7].
Missing number in any position: 8 + ? = 11, 7 = ? - 9 [eng-pos], 8 + 4 = ? + 5 [nrich-bal].
13 + 24 = 12 + 25: explain without computing both sides [eng-pos Y5 notes].
Write an equation for a story; several equations may fit [im-g1].
Needed later: algebraic notation and linear equations (brief later_concepts); equivalent expressions [ccss-6ee].

curriculum: Common Core, opened: 1.OA.B.3 apply commutative and associative properties as strategies, formal terms not required; 3.OA.B.5 commutative, associative and distributive properties as strategies for multiplication and division with footnote that formal terms are not needed [ccss-1oa, ccss-3oa]. 2.NBT.B.5-6 and B.9 ask pupils to justify methods with properties of operations [ccss-2nbt]; 3.OA.D.9 explains table patterns with properties [ccss-3oa]. Brief codes confirmed.

England PoS, opened: Year 2 statutory show that adding two numbers can be done in any order (commutative) but subtraction cannot, same for multiplication versus division; notes say pupils check addition by reordering which establishes commutativity and associativity; Year 3 notes use these for mental multiplication; Year 4 notes associativity and distributivity. Identity: Year 1 notes say adding or subtracting 0 has no effect. Inverse: Year 2 statutory inverse relation of addition and subtraction [eng-pos]. Brief's 'Y2, Y4' is right (also Y1 identity, Y3 notes).
Korea: not opened (no code in brief).
textbooks: IM Grade 1 Unit 3 and 5 use properties implicitly (making ten, adding by place) [im-g1]. IM Grade 3 Unit 1 Section C arrays and the commutative property; Unit 4 commutativity links fact pairs, associativity appears when multiplying by multiples of 10, children are not asked to name properties [im-g3].
OpenStax Prealgebra 2e 1.3/1.5: identity and commutative property of addition; zero, identity and commutative of multiplication [os-add, os-mul].

OpenStax Prealgebra 2e Ch.7 'Commutative and Associative Properties': addition and multiplication are commutative but subtraction and division are not; grouping may be changed for three or more terms; use to regroup for easier calculation, for example pairing opposites or reciprocals [os-comm].

OpenStax Prealgebra 2e Ch.7 'Properties of Identity, Inverse and Zero': 0 additive identity, 1 multiplicative identity; opposite as additive inverse; reciprocal as multiplicative inverse; x * 0 = 0; 0 divided by nonzero is 0; division by zero undefined; summary table of properties [os-ident]. (The adjacent module m81315 is Rational and Irrational Numbers, not properties.)
explanations: Reordering to check sums, swapping addends, regrouping addends to make ten: [ccss-1oa 1.OA.B.3], [eng-pos].
Arrays, rows versus columns give the same product (commutative multiplication): [os-mul], [im-g3 Unit 1].
One multiplication equation read as 'groups of' in two ways: [ncetm-comm].
Doubling and halving as inverses; ten times table is double the five times table: [ncetm-comm].
Symbolic statements of the laws with letters: a(b+c) = ab+ac in Y5 notes [eng-pos]; commutative/associative with variables [os-comm].
Inverse as undoing: subtraction undoes addition, division undoes multiplication: [os-div], [eng-pos].
conventions: Formal names are not required in CCSS (1.OA.B.3 and 3.OA.B.5 footnote) and IM does not ask children to name them [ccss-1oa, ccss-3oa, im-g3]; England's PoS does use the word commutative in the Year 2 statutory text [eng-pos].
OpenStax gives names plus symbols; the Y5 England notes write a(b+c) = ab+ac [os-comm, eng-pos].
'Associative/associativity' appears as a note in England Y2-Y4 [eng-pos].
Korean terms (교환법칙, 결합법칙, 분배법칙) from memory, unverified.
misconceptions: Subtraction and division are not commutative; this is stated explicitly in England Y2 and OpenStax [eng-pos, os-comm].
Inferring a property from one example is not proof; CCSS 2.NBT.B.9 and 3.OA.D.9 ask pupils to explain why using the properties [ccss-2nbt, ccss-3oa].
NCETM segment 2.10 aims to explain why multiplication can be done in either order but division cannot [ncetm-dist].
Grouping change versus order change are different properties; OpenStax separates commutative (order) from associative (grouping) [os-comm].
Teaching advice: let children discover and use properties as strategies before naming them [ccss-3oa footnote, im-g3].
tasks: Swap addends and check 3 + 5 = 5 + 3 with objects; counterexample 5 - 3 versus 3 - 5; 6 / 3 versus 3 / 6 [eng-pos].
Regroup to make ten: 7 + 3 + 5; 2 + 6 + 8 [ccss-1oa].
Use x + 0, x * 1, x * 0 [os-ident]; additive inverse x + (-x) = 0 and reciprocal [os-ident].
Reorder a product 4 * 7 * 25 to calculate [os-comm style].
Needed later: distributive-property; rings and algebraic structures in Looking ahead (identity, inverse, commutative, associative are ring axioms; wording from field knowledge, unverified).

curriculum: Common Core, opened: 2.OA.C.4 arrays with up to 5 rows and columns, total as repeated addition; 3.OA.A.1 meaning of a product as groups; 3.OA.A.3 word problems with equal groups, arrays, measurement quantities within 100; 3.OA.A.4 unknown in a multiplication equation; 3.OA.B.5 properties as strategies; 3.OA.C.7 fluency within 100 and memory of all one-digit products by end of Grade 3; 3.OA.D.9 patterns in the multiplication table [ccss-2oa, ccss-3oa]. 3.NBT.A.3 one-digit by multiple of ten; 4.NBT.B.5 multi-digit by one-digit and 2x2 using place value and area models, arrays or equations (no standard algorithm named) [ccss-3nbt, ccss-4nbt]. 4.OA.A.1-2 (multiplicative comparison) not opened here: unverified.
Brief's code '3.OA.A.1,3' and others confirmed; 3.MD.C.7 (area) listed under distributive-property.

England PoS, opened: Y1 solve one-step multiplication/division with objects, pictures, arrays, teacher support; Y2 tables for 2, 5, 10, commutative; arrays, repeated addition; Y3 tables 3, 4, 8, 2-digit by 1-digit with mental then formal methods; Y4 tables to 12x12 (the text summary said distributive law, factor pairs, 2- and 3-digit by 1-digit formal layout); Y5 up to four digits by one or two digits, long multiplication for 2-digit; Y6 four digits by two-digit with long multiplication, order of operations [eng-pos]. Table-by-year detail beyond what was returned (tables to 12 in Y4) is unverified.
Korea 2022 [2수01-08..09], [4수01-03]: not opened; unverified.
textbooks: IM Grade 3 Unit 1 Introducing Multiplication: scaled picture/bar graphs with scales 2, 5, 10; B multiplication as equal groups; C arrays and the commutative property; tape diagrams, discrete drawings, equations as number of groups times size of group [im-g3]. Glossary: array, factor, product, multiplication (total of a number of equal groups), expression, equation [im-g3u1gl].
IM Grade 3 Unit 4: multiply 1- and 2-digit numbers, decompose a factor 7*3 = (5*3)+(2*3), area models with partitioned rectangles, parentheses [im-g3].

OpenStax Prealgebra 2e 1.5 Multiply Whole Numbers: repeated addition, rows of pennies 8+8+8 = 3*8, counters as arrays; factors and product; symbols x, dot, parentheses; zero and identity and commutative properties; multi-digit by partial products with placeholder zeros; powers of 10; three factors two at a time; key words times, product of, twice [os-mul].

NCETM Spine 2 (Year 2 to 6): 2.2 structures as equal groups, 2.3-2.5 tables for 2, 10, 5 and commutativity, 2.7-2.9 tables 2/4/8, 3/6/9, 7, 2.14 partitioning for multiplication leading to short multiplication, 2.23 long multiplication [ncetm-md].
explanations: Equal groups with objects and drawings; tape diagrams: [im-g3].
Repeated addition and skip counting: [os-mul], [ccss-2oa 2.OA.C.4], [eng-pos Y2].
Arrays (rows and columns, counters); same product counting rows or columns: [os-mul], [im-g3], [eng-pos Y1 arrays and counting in 2s, 5s, 10s].
Area of rectangle tiled by unit squares: [ccss-3md 3.MD.C.7a-b].
Scaled picture and bar graphs as a bridge from counting in 2s, 5s, 10s: [im-g3].
Partial products / partitioning one factor, long multiplication layout: [os-mul], [ncetm-md], [eng-pos].
Number line jumps of equal size: not found in opened sources (unverified).
conventions: Writing a x b: IM writes number of groups times size of each group [im-g3]; whether 3 x 8 means 3 groups of 8 or 8 groups of 3 differs by country: unverified (CCSS 3.OA.A.1 example 5 x 7 as 5 groups of 7 [ccss-3oa]).
Symbols: x, dot and parentheses [os-mul]. The asterisk and the Korean 곱하기 / 배: unverified.
Terms: factor, product (OpenStax, IM) [os-mul, im-g3u1gl]; 'times tables' (England) versus 'multiplication table' (CCSS wording 3.OA.D.9) [eng-pos, ccss-3oa].
Layout: OpenStax vertical with partial products and placeholder zeros; England names short multiplication and long multiplication [os-mul, eng-pos].
Korean multiplication table 구구단 (up to 9 x 9) and number words 일이삼 / 하나둘셋: unverified.
misconceptions: Multiplication always makes bigger (and division smaller): false for factors below 1 or zero; a prospective-teacher study used prediction and clickers to address it [lim].
CCSS expects pupils to explain products as groups, not only to recall: 3.OA.A.1 [ccss-3oa].
Commutativity: groups-of reading changes (2 groups of 5 versus 5 groups of 2) while the total stays the same [ncetm-comm, im-g3].
Zero and one as factors need explicit teaching: segment 2.4 'factors of 0 and 1' [ncetm-md]; OpenStax states x*0 = 0, x*1 = x [os-mul].
Unequal groups cannot be multiplied as equal groups; IM glossary requires equal rows in an array [im-g3u1gl].
tasks: How many in 4 groups of 6; arrays 3 x 5; write repeated addition equation for array [ccss-2oa, os-mul].
Missing factor 8 * ? = 48 [ccss-3oa 3.OA.A.4].
Scaled picture graph questions [im-g3].
Facts to 10 x 10 from memory by end of Grade 3; patterns in the table e.g. multiples of 4 are even [ccss-3oa 3.OA.C.7, D.9].
Multi-digit: 2-digit by 1-digit with decomposing (7 x 3 = 5x3 + 2x3), then partial products [im-g3, os-mul].
Needed later: division as missing factor, distributive property, area, factors-multiples, powers, multiplying fractions, ratio (brief later_concepts).

curriculum: Common Core, opened: 3.OA.A.2 meaning of quotient as share size or number of groups; 3.OA.A.3 word problems within 100; 3.OA.A.4 unknown in a division equation; 3.OA.B.6 division as an unknown-factor problem; 3.OA.C.7 fluency within 100; 3.OA.B.5 properties; 4.NBT.B.6 divide up to four-digit dividends by one-digit divisors with remainders using place value, properties and the relation to multiplication, shown with equations, arrays or area models (no standard algorithm named) [ccss-3oa, ccss-4nbt]. Brief's '3.OA.A.2,4, 3.OA.B.6' confirmed; 4.NBT.B.6 should be added.

England PoS, opened: Y1 sharing/grouping problems with objects, pictures, arrays; Y2 division not commutative, solve with arrays, repeated addition and facts; Y3 progress to short division in notes; Y4 short division in notes; Y5 divide up to four digits by one digit using short division, inverse use; Y6 long division by two-digit numbers and short division where appropriate [eng-pos]. Brief's 'Y2-Y5' should extend to Y6 for long division (separate concept).
Korea 2022 [4수01-04..06]: not opened; unverified.
textbooks: IM Grade 3 Unit 4 Relating Multiplication to Division: A 'how many groups' and 'how many in each group'; B division as missing factor and fact fluency; C multiply 1- and 2-digit numbers; D divide larger numbers; equal-group drawings, arrays, area models, equations with parentheses [im-g3]. Unit 1 previews division with missing-factor problems [im-g3].

OpenStax Prealgebra 2e 1.6 Divide Whole Numbers: repeated subtraction (12 cookies into bags of 4), division undoes multiplication; notation with divide sign, slash, fraction bar and long-division bracket; dividend, divisor, quotient, remainder; counters modelling; check by multiplying and adding the remainder; special cases n/n = 1, n/1 = n, 0/n = 0 and n/0 undefined; long division with divide-multiply-subtract-bring-down; examples 78/3, 2596/4, 1439/4 = 359 R3, 74521/241 = 309 R52 [os-div].

NCETM segments 2.6 quotitive and partitive division, 2.10 connecting multiplication and division, 2.12 division with remainders, 2.15 partitioning for division leading to short division [ncetm-md, ncetm-quot, ncetm-dist].
explanations: Sharing (partitive): known number of shares, find share size; grouping (quotitive): known group size, find number of groups; both solved by skip counting or known facts: [ncetm-quot], [ccss-3oa 3.OA.A.2].
Repeated subtraction: [os-div].
Missing-factor reading (32 / 8 asks 8 x ? = 32): [ccss-3oa 3.OA.B.6], [im-g3].
Counters in groups, leftover as remainder: [os-div], [ncetm-quot].
Arrays and area models for division: [im-g3], [ccss-4nbt 4.NBT.B.6].
Halving as division by two: [ncetm-quot].
Long and short division layouts: [os-div], [eng-pos].
conventions: Division signs: divide sign, slash, fraction bar, bracket (OpenStax) [os-div]; the colon sign used in some countries: unverified.
Names: dividend, divisor, quotient, remainder [os-div]; 'quotitive/partitive' (NCETM) versus 'how many groups / how many in each group' (IM) versus 'sharing/grouping' [ncetm-quot, im-g3].

Layout: short division (bus-stop style in England, name 'short division' only seen in PoS) versus long division bracket in OpenStax [eng-pos, os-div]; the Korean written layout 나눗셈 세로식 and terms 몫, 나머지: unverified.
Remainder notation: 'R3' used by OpenStax [os-div].
misconceptions: Division makes smaller: false in general (dividing by numbers below 1) [lim].
Division is not commutative; 12 / 3 differs from 3 / 12 [eng-pos Y2, ncetm-dist].
Two structures look the same in symbols (12 / 4) but are different situations; teach both [ncetm-quot].
Division by zero is undefined, because no number times zero gives a nonzero dividend; 0 / n is 0 [os-div, ncetm-quot].
Remainders: check as quotient x divisor + remainder = dividend [os-div].
Teaching advice: use known multiplication facts rather than only skip counting, and link the two operations [ncetm-quot, ccss-3oa 3.OA.B.6].
tasks: Share 12 into 3 equal groups; make groups of 4 from 12 [os-div, ncetm-quot].
Find 32 / 8 as 8 x ? = 32 [ccss-3oa].
Word problems with equal groups / arrays / measurement within 100 [ccss-3oa 3.OA.A.3].
Division with remainder: 1439 / 4 = 359 R3 [os-div].
Check by multiplication [os-div].

Needed later: long division, order of operations, factors-multiples, fractions-meaning (a/b as division), dividing fractions, mean (brief later_concepts); 2.26 mean and equal shares in NCETM Y6 [ncetm-md].

curriculum: Common Core, opened: 3.OA.B.5 distributive property as strategy, formal term not required [ccss-3oa]; 3.MD.C.7c use tiling to show a x (b+c) equals a x b + a x c, area models for the distributive property; 3.MD.C.7d area is additive [ccss-3md]; 4.NBT.B.5-6 area models and place value with properties [ccss-4nbt]; 6.EE.A.3 apply properties such as the distributive property to produce equivalent expressions [ccss-6ee]. Brief's codes confirmed.

England PoS, opened: Year 4 statutory 'use the distributive law to multiply two-digit numbers by one digit' (in the summary returned) and notes on associativity and distributivity; Year 5 notes state a(b+c) = ab+ac; Year 6 no separate statement found [eng-pos]. Brief says 'Y4, Y6': Y5 notes is the explicit symbolic one; Y6 not confirmed.
Korea: no code in brief; not opened.
textbooks: IM Grade 3 Unit 4: decomposing a factor, 7*3 = (5*3) + (2*3), builds intuition; area models with partitioned rectangles; students are not asked to name the property [im-g3].

OpenStax Prealgebra 2e Ch.7 Distributive Property: movie-ticket money example, a(b+c) = ab+ac, a(b-c) = ab-ac, (b+c)a = ba+ca; examples 3(x+4) = 3x+12, 2(x-3) = 2x-6, -2(4y+1) = -8y-2, -(y+5) = -y-5, 8-2(x+3) = -2x+2; evaluate before and after distributing to see equal values [os-dist].

NCETM segment 2.10 Year 4: uses the gap between neighbouring multiples to introduce the law, understood as splitting the number of groups; also solving two-part problems that add or subtract products sharing a factor [ncetm-dist].
OpenStax Elementary Algebra 1.9 cited in brief: not opened; unverified.
explanations: Array or area model split into two rectangles: [ccss-3md 3.MD.C.7c], [im-g3 area models].
Equal groups split: 7 groups = 5 groups + 2 groups: [ncetm-dist], [im-g3].
Money example (price of several tickets of two kinds): [os-dist].
Symbolic a(b+c) = ab+ac with letters, extended to subtraction and negatives: [os-dist], [eng-pos Y5].
Evaluate both forms for a number to confirm equal value: [os-dist].
Place-value partition for multiplying (e.g. 23 x 4 as 20 x 4 + 3 x 4): [ccss-4nbt 4.NBT.B.5], [eng-pos].
conventions: Name: distributive property (US, CCSS, OpenStax) versus distributive law (England PoS and NCETM) [os-dist, eng-pos, ncetm-dist].
Brackets/parentheses: parentheses in IM and CCSS; brackets in England: [im-g3, eng-pos Y6 order of operations note].
Writing the product as juxtaposition ab in algebra versus x in arithmetic: [os-dist].
Left- and right-handed forms: a(b+c) and (b+c)a [os-dist].
Korean 분배법칙: unverified.
misconceptions: Distributing over subtraction and over negative factors are common slips, and the sign of every term must be changed with a negative multiplier (-(y+5) = -y-5): examples in OpenStax, no explicit misconception text [os-dist].
Distributive property is not applied to a product inside brackets in the same way (a(bc) is not ab x ac); common error cited in the literature, but unverified in opened pages.

Division distributes over a sum only from the right: (a+b)/c = a/c + b/c, but c/(a+b) is not c/a + c/b; not found in opened pages, unverified. NCETM stresses that multiplication is commutative while division is not [ncetm-dist].
Teaching advice: build from arrays/area, then number facts, then letters; names are optional early [ccss-3oa footnote, im-g3, ncetm-dist].
tasks: Split an array: 7 x 6 = 5 x 6 + 2 x 6; draw and count [im-g3, ccss-3md].
Area of a rectangle with sides 4 and (3+5) [ccss-3md 3.MD.C.7c].
Mental multiplication: 14 x 5, 99 x 6 as (100-1) x 6 [os-dist subtraction form].
Expand and simplify 3(x+4), 2(x-3), -2(4y+1) [os-dist].
Needed later: long multiplication, surds, equivalent expressions (brief later_concepts), 6.EE.A.3 [ccss-6ee].
